analysis.investment_thesis: A tiny ₹338 Cr IT-enabled services outfit with decent headline ROE/ROCE (28%/26%) but rapidly deteriorating capital discipline — borrowings jumped from ₹6 Cr to ₹28 Cr in two years while FCF collapsed from ₹10 Cr to zero. At 35x P/E for a sub-scale, undifferentiated services business with no visible moat, the price embeds growth that the cash flows do not support.
key_strengths: Reported ROE 28.2% and ROCE 26.5% — optically attractive on a small base
Revenue grew 70% over two years (₹73 Cr → ₹124 Cr) with margins expanding (operating margin ~11%)
Promoter holding 54.73% provides skin in the game
key_risks: FCF deteriorated from ₹10 Cr (2023) to ₹0 Cr (2025); cumulative 3Y FCF negative — earnings quality is poor
Borrowings 4.6x in two years (₹6 Cr → ₹28 Cr); equity raise + debt funding growth, not internal accruals
Generic 'customer transformation' IT services — no discernible moat, competing against thousands of similar shops
red_flags: Net profit ₹10 Cr vs Operating CF ₹13 Cr looks fine in 2025, but 3Y aggregate FCF is roughly zero against ₹20 Cr cumulative profits — earnings not converting to cash
Total assets nearly tripled (₹35 → ₹99 Cr) in 2 years funded by debt + equity issuance, not retained earnings
Recently listed micro-cap (BSE SME-style) — limited audit history, low float, vulnerable to promoter actions
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Invert first: what kills this investment? A small IT services firm growing by piling on debt and external equity, where the high ROE is a function of recent capital infusions not yet fully deployed, and where free cash flow has gone from ₹10 Cr to negative ₹20 Cr to zero in three years. The ROCE of 26% is arithmetic; the economic reality is that the business consumed roughly all the cash it generated. That is the opposite of a compounding machine — that is a treadmill. At 35x earnings on ₹10 Cr of profit, you are paying ₹338 Cr for a business whose owner-earnings are functionally zero.

The "customer transformation partner" descriptor is the kind of vague positioning that screams commodity services. There is no proprietary IP, no switching costs evident, no network effect — just bodies billed against client projects in a brutally competitive space dominated by TCS, Infosys, and a thousand mid-tier shops. Promoter holding at 54.73% is acceptable but unremarkable for a recent listing. I want to see five years of clean cash conversion, ROIC sustained above 20% through a downturn, and a clearly articulated competitive advantage before paying anywhere near 35x. None of those tests are met. Pass.
